mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 5.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 5.0% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate falling below 4.5% signals robust labor market conditions that increase consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 0.5%+ monthly increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS rise > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 100 signals weakening economic output, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during supply chain disruptions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 1600 units indicates strong residential construction demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1600 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL rising above 202.0 indicates accelerating inflation that triggers central bank rate hikes, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 202.0 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent 0.5%+ payroll growth (PAYEMS) and 0.2pp+ unemployment decline (UNRATE) in one month signal labor market tightening that boosts consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls < 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when both PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls < 0.2pp (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales exceeding 350,000 million dollars indicates sustained consumer spending growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days during retail expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when RSAFS > 350,000 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).
